title: Size of an affine scheme
statement: Let $Y$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $A=\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$ be its ring of global sections [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Using the cardinal size [def-sfb-scheme-cardinal-size], for a scheme $Z$ put $s(Z)=\max\{\aleph_0,|\mathcal B(Z)|,\sup_{V\in\mathcal B(Z)}|\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_Z)|\}$, where $\mathcal B(Z)$ is the set of affine open subschemes and $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_Z)$ is the ring of sections of the structure sheaf on $V$. Then $s(Y)=\max\{\aleph_0,|A|\}$. The zero ring and the empty affine scheme are allowed.

source.place: Tag 000P, lemma-bound-affine; scheme size defined in section-categories-schemes preceding Tag 000I.

proof.text: Put $\kappa=\max\{\aleph_0,|A|\}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-spec-points] to the top affine open of $Y$ to identify $Y$ with $\operatorname{Spec}A$. A scheme isomorphism gives a bijection on affine opens and, by the inverse maps of structure sheaves, ring isomorphisms on their sections, so it preserves $s$. Since $Y$ itself is an affine open, the definition [def-sfb-scheme-cardinal-size] gives $s(Y)\geq\kappa$.

source.place: Tag 000P, lemma-bound-affine, proof; section-categories-schemes defines size.

proof.text: For an affine open $U\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}A$, [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open](i) gives the covering by those $D(f)$ contained in $U$. The affine scheme $U$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]; by [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] this cover has a finite subcover, say $U=D(f_1)\cup\cdots\cup D(f_n)$. The empty list is allowed when $U=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 000P, lemma-bound-affine, proof; section-categories-schemes defines size.

proof.text: Assign to each finite list $(f_1,\ldots,f_n)$ its union of principal opens. Step 2 says every affine open is among these images. Hence the set of affine opens has cardinal at most $|\operatorname{List}(A)|\leq\kappa$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-list-cardinality]. Lists whose union is not affine cause no problem: restrict the domain to lists with affine union to obtain a surjection onto the affine opens.

source.place: Tag 000P, lemma-bound-affine, proof; section-categories-schemes defines size.

proof.text: Let $f_1,\ldots,f_n\in A$ with $n\geq0$. By [def-weil-ring-localization-away] every element of $A_{f_i}$ is a fraction $a/f_i^{m}$, and $a/f_i^{m}=af_i^{k}/f_i^{m+k}$ for every $k\geq0$; taking the largest exponent and multiplying the numerators, every element of $\prod_{i=1}^nA_{f_i}$ is $(a_1/f_1^{m},\ldots,a_n/f_n^{m})$ with one common exponent $m\geq0$. Hence the map sending a list $(a_1,\ldots,a_n,b_1,\ldots,b_m)$ of elements of $A$ of length $n+m\geq n$ to $(a_1/f_1^{m},\ldots,a_n/f_n^{m})$ is a surjection from a subset of $\operatorname{List}(A)$ onto $\prod_{i=1}^nA_{f_i}$, and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-list-cardinality] gives $|\prod_{i=1}^nA_{f_i}|\leq|\operatorname{List}(A)|\leq\kappa$. For $n=1$ this is the bound $|A_f|\leq\kappa$ omitted in the source; for $n=0$ the product is a singleton. No hypothesis on $A$ or on the $f_i$ (nilpotents, $f_i=0$) is used.

source.place: Tag 000P, lemma-bound-affine, proof; section-categories-schemes defines size.

proof.text: For the cover in step 2, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime](b) identifies $\Gamma(D(f_i),\mathcal O)$ with $A_{f_i}$. The structure sheaf is a sheaf of rings by [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism]. Its additive sheaf satisfies the uniqueness axiom for the open cover, as in [def-sc-zariski-site]: two sections with the same restrictions agree. Thus restriction is injective into $\prod_{i=1}^n A_{f_i}$. Step 4 bounds this product by $\kappa$, so $|\Gamma(U,\mathcal O)|\leq\kappa$. For $n=0$, the sheaf axiom on the empty cover makes $\Gamma(\varnothing,\mathcal O)$ a singleton, agreeing with the empty product.

source.place: Tag 000P, lemma-bound-affine, proof; section-categories-schemes defines size.

proof.text: Steps 3 and 5 bound both cardinal contributions in [def-sfb-scheme-cardinal-size] by $\kappa$; also $\aleph_0\leq\kappa$. Therefore $s(Y)\leq\kappa$, and step 1 gives equality. If $A$ is the zero ring, its spectrum is empty, its only open is empty and the sections on it form the singleton zero ring; both sides are $\aleph_0$.
